authoredSolutions.27: The figure shows the unsaturated (enol) ether \(CH_{3}-CH=CH-O-C(CH_{3})=CH_{2}\). Acidic hydrolysis cleaves the \(C-O\) bonds of an enol ether and each fragment is released as an enol that tautomerises to a carbonyl compound. The fragment \(CH_{3}-CH=CH-OH\) tautomerises to propanal, \(CH_{3}CH_{2}CHO\) (P), and the fragment \(CH_{2}=C(CH_{3})-OH\) tautomerises to propanone, \(CH_{3}COCH_{3}\) (Q). To distinguish an aliphatic aldehyde from a ketone, Fehling solution is the correct choice: propanal reduces it to a red-brown \(Cu_{2}O\) precipitate while acetone gives no reaction. The other reagents fail: 2,4-DNP gives an orange precipitate with both; saturated \(NaHSO_{3}\) forms a bisulphite adduct with aldehydes and also with methyl ketones such as acetone; Lucas reagent is a test for alcohols, not carbonyls.
